To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the emplacement of magmas in the middle crust leads to the formation and growth of an anatexic dome.

the composition of plutons is the result of the composition of the source and the conditions of magma extraction, whereas the composition of the dome is controlled by the composition of the plutons that are accumulated in its core.

(1) anatectic melts form plutons and anatexis can form an anatectic core in an anatexis dome; (2) the composition of plutonic and dome anatectic magmas is controlled by the type of melting reactions; (3) the emplacement of magmas at deeper level enhances melting and the formation of anatexis domes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of anatexis in the crust during collision and subsequent orogenic collapse.
the formation of anatectic dome and plutons in the SE-FMC.
the formation of plutons and domes and their consequences on the behaviour of continental crust.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

anatectic magmas extracted at high pressure and temperature (hot-and-dry) are more likely to form plutons than domes, while those extracted at low pressure and temperature (cool-and-wet) are more likely form domes.
plutons are formed by the extraction of melt in the crust whereas the formation of anatectic dome is the consequence of the retention of magmas during the extraction.
plutons and domes are two different ways to form anatectic magmas and that the emplacement of an anatectic dome has a major effect on the behaviour of continental crust during orogeny.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anatectic magmas are formed in two distinct ways, depending on the temperature of the source.
the emplacement of anatectic plutons is controlled by the composition of the source material, the temperature and the pressure conditions.

plutons are formed by magmas that are produced by melting of lower-crustal material, whereas the core of an anatexic dome forms by in-situ melting of the lower crust triggered by magmatic underplating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anatectic magmas may form plutons or domes and that the resulting magmas have distinct chemical compositions and distinct implications on the evolution of the continental crust.
the emplacement of magmas in plutons or in domes has different consequences on the behaviour of crust.

anatectic magmas may be produced by dehydration melting of muscovite or biotite, but the type of melt (cool-and-wet versus hot-and-dry), the amount of melt, the composition of the melt and the composition of the residue are all controlled by the temperature of melting.
